name: Tirhakah
title: King of Cush
summary: Tirhakah (also known as Taharqa) was king of Cush (Ethiopia/Nubia) and a pharaoh in Egypt's 25th dynasty. He is mentioned in the Bible in connection with his military campaign against the Assyrian king Sennacherib, when he came to help King Hezekiah of Judah against the Assyrian threat.

keyEvents.title: Tirhakah's Campaign Against Sennacherib
keyEvents.description: Sennacherib, king of Assyria, received word that Tirhakah, king of Cush, had set out to fight against him. This occurred during Sennacherib's siege of Judah.

keyEvents.title: Sennacherib's Threat Against Hezekiah
keyEvents.description: After hearing about Tirhakah's advance, Sennacherib sent messengers to King Hezekiah with a threatening letter to warn him not to trust in God's deliverance.

keyEvents.title: Hezekiah's Prayer for Deliverance
keyEvents.description: When King Hezekiah received Sennacherib's threatening letter, he went up to the house of the Lord and prayed for God's help against the Assyrian threat, in a context where Tirhakah's military presence also played a role.

keyEvents.title: Isaiah's Prophecy about the Fall of Sennacherib
keyEvents.description: The prophet Isaiah conveyed God's answer to Hezekiah and prophesied that Sennacherib would not capture Jerusalem but be driven back—a situation where Tirhakah's threat from the south also contributed to pressure on Assyria.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of the Assyrian Army
keyEvents.description: The Lord's angel struck the Assyrian camp at night and killed 185,000 soldiers, causing Sennacherib to retreat. Tirhakah's military pressure from the south, together with God's intervention, defeated the Assyrian threat.
